messages:
Ana (Product): Quick post-all-hands: teams asked for crisp guidance on three things — 1) where to bias investment across Hosted/Dedicated/Private this year, 2) a single sentence SDR pitch for Dedicated, and 3) how we should position vs cloud bundles and DIY runtimes in one line.

Jordan (CEO): Short answers: mission unchanged  make inference dependable and cost-transparent for builders. Investment posture: prioritize Hosted (growth + fast iteration), keep Dedicated funded for enterprise monetization and SLA work, and treat Private as strategic/resourced per-deal. We won't stop Dedicated work; we'll sequence priorities so Hosted features land faster.

Evan (Eng): For planning, does "sequence" mean Dedicated delivery timelines shift or just fewer new experiments? Need dev planning clarity.

Jordan (CEO): Fewer new experiments on Dedicated; critical stability/SLA work continues. New platform innovations default to Hosted first and then port to Dedicated with opt-in flags where behavior could change.

Rita (Sales): For SDRs: what's a 10-second pitch to qualify for Dedicated?

Jordan (CEO): Use this: "If you need SLA-backed throughput, predictable unit cost, or private network controls, ask us about Dedicated capacity." Short, signal-focused.

Ana (Product): And the competitor one-liner? Something neutral we can put in decks.

Jordan (CEO): Try: "Redwood turns models into production-ready inference across hosted, reserved, and private deployments — predictable latency, transparent costs, and operational controls without rebuilding ops." Keep it factual; tailor tone for dev vs exec audiences.

Evan (Eng): Action items for Eng: I'll propose three SLO buckets (p50/p95 latency, cold-start, cost/token) and an opt-in compatibility rubric for behavior-changing runtime changes by next Tue.

Rita (Sales): I'll add Jordan's SDR pitch and the one-liner to the playbook as provisional copy and loop RevOps on threshold numbers.

NotesBot: All-hands recording + slides uploaded: https://redwood.internal/recordings/2366008888 — notes in the shared drive.

Ana (Product): Thanks all. Drop follow-ups here or DM me.
